title: Universal property and uniqueness of sheafified free modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings and $E$ a sheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$. Write $|M|$ for the underlying sheaf of sets of a module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Define $B[E]$ as the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of $U\mapsto B(U)[E(U)]$, the free module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with restrictions $\sum b_e[e]\mapsto\sum(b_e|_V)[e|_V]$, and let $i_{B,E}:E\to|B[E]|$ be induced by $e\mapsto[e]$. For every $B$-module sheaf $M$, restriction to generators is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_B(B[E],M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(E,|M|)$, $h\mapsto |h|\circ i_{B,E}$, natural in $E$ and $M$. Its inverse extends $a:E\to|M|$ by the sectionwise formula $\sum b_e[e]\mapsto\sum b_ea(e)$ followed by module sheafification. More generally, if a $B$-module sheaf $P$ with $k:E\to|P|$ has bijective restrictions $\operatorname{Hom}_B(P,M)\to\operatorname{Hom}(E,|M|)$ for all $M$, then there is a unique isomorphism $p:P\xrightarrow{\sim}B[E]$ with $|p|\circ k=i_{B,E}$; its inverse is the unique map $q$ with $|q|\circ i_{B,E}=k$.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, proof: construction of O_2[F] and extension of maps from its generators; normalized-realization uniqueness is the universal-property consequence.

proof.text: Put $F_E(U)=B(U)[E(U)]$, realized as finitely supported coefficient families on $E(U)$, with basis $[e]$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. For $v:V\to U$, send $\sum_e b_e[e]$ to $\sum_e(b_e|_v)[e|_v]$; repeated restricted indices are combined by addition. This is well-defined since the family has finite support. It is additive and semilinear: restricting $c\sum b_e[e]$ gives $\sum(c|_v)(b_e|_v)[e|_v]$. Identity and composite restrictions agree on each $[e]$ and each coefficient, hence on every finite sum. Thus $F_E$ is a presheaf of $B$-modules. The maps $e\mapsto[e]$ commute with restriction; composing them with the module-sheafification unit $\eta_E:F_E\to B[E]$ gives the stated $i_{B,E}$.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, proof, free-module construction and generator formulas; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, universal factorization.

proof.text: Given $a:E\to|M|$, define $T_{a,U}(\sum_e b_e[e])=\sum_e b_ea_U(e)$. Unique finite basis expansions make this well-defined, additive and $B(U)$-linear. For $v:V\to U$, semilinearity in $M$ and naturality of $a$ give $(\sum_e b_ea_U(e))|_v=\sum_e(b_e|_v)a_V(e|_v)$, exactly $T_{a,V}$ of the restricted input. Hence $T_a:F_E\to M$ is a module-presheaf morphism. Every such morphism is determined by its values on the basis, because $T_U(\sum b_e[e])=\sum b_eT_U([e])$. Conversely its basis values form a presheaf map $E\to|M|$ by restriction compatibility. Since $E$ and $|M|$ are sheaves, these are precisely maps of sheaves of sets.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, proof, free-module construction and generator formulas; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, universal factorization.

proof.text: Apply the universal factorization stated in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] to $T_a$ and the $B$-module sheaf $M$. There is a unique $B$-linear sheaf morphism $\widehat a:B[E]\to M$ satisfying $\widehat a\eta_E=T_a$. On a generator this equality says $|\widehat a|i_{B,E}(e)=a(e)$. This constructs the inverse of restriction to generators, with exactly the sectionwise formula in the statement. The sheafification is of a module presheaf over the already given ring sheaf $B$, so no change of coefficient ring is involved.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, proof, free-module construction and generator formulas; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, universal factorization.

proof.text: For $h:B[E]\to M$ let $a=|h|i_{B,E}$. The two maps $h\eta_E$ and $T_a$ agree on every $[e]$, and by linearity on every finite sum. The uniqueness of factorization through $\eta_E$ therefore gives $h=\widehat a$. Together with the generator equality of step 3 this proves both inverse identities and the asserted bijection. In particular two maps out of $B[E]$ are equal whenever their composites with $i_{B,E}$ agree; this does not require $\eta_E(U)$ to be surjective on sections.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, proof, free-module construction and generator formulas; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, universal factorization.

proof.text: For $f:E\to E\prime$, define $F_f:F_E\to F_{E\prime}$ on a finite sum by $\sum_e b_e[e]\mapsto\sum_e b_e[f_U(e)]$. Additivity, semilinearity of restrictions and $f_V(e|_v)=f_U(e)|_v$ show it is a module-presheaf map. Sheafify to obtain $B[f]:B[E]\to B[E\prime]$ with $|B[f]|i_{B,E}=i_{B,E\prime}f$. Identity and composite maps satisfy this same formula and hence agree by step 4, so this construction is functorial. Write $R_{E,M}(h)=|h|i_{B,E}$. For $g:M\to M\prime$ one has $R_{E,M\prime}(g h)=|g|R_{E,M}(h)$, and for $h:B[E\prime]\to M$ one has $R_{E,M}(h B[f])=R_{E\prime,M}(h)f$. These follow by substitution of the displayed generator identity and associativity. They prove naturality in both variables; the inverse bijections are natural by applying these equalities and injectivity.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, proof, free-module construction and generator formulas; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, universal factorization.

proof.text: Finally suppose $(P,k)$ has the stated universal property. Its bijection at $M=B[E]$ supplies a unique $p:P\to B[E]$ with $|p|k=i_{B,E}$. The bijection just proved for $B[E]$, at $M=P$, supplies a unique $q:B[E]\to P$ with $|q|i_{B,E}=k$. Then $|qp|k=|q|i_{B,E}=k=|\mathrm{id}_P|k$, so injectivity of the assumed restriction map at $M=P$ gives $qp=\mathrm{id}_P$. Similarly $|pq|i_{B,E}=|p|k=i_{B,E}$ and step 4 gives $pq=\mathrm{id}_{B[E]}$. Thus $p$ is an isomorphism with inverse $q$. Any isomorphism obeying the same generator equation has underlying map $p$ by the assumed injectivity, which proves uniqueness of the normalized isomorphism as well as the stated characterization of its inverse.
